children: Nomura retained its 'Buy' ratings on M&M, Hyundai Motor India, Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles (TMCV), TVS Motor and Sonacom after August wholesale volumes showed strong demand across auto segments. MHCVs were the biggest positive surprise, while TMCV and Bajaj Auto were well ahead of estimates. Nomura retained 'Neutral' on Maruti Suzuki, Ashok Leyland, Hero MotoCorp and Eicher Motors.

August wholesale volumes rose 36% year-on-year (y-y) for passenger vehicles (PVs), 10% for two-wheelers, 9% for tractors and 35% for medium and heavy commercial vehicles (MHCVs), versus Nomura estimates of 41%, 11%, 6% and 25%, respectively.

"Strong demand momentum" continued across auto segments, Nomura said, with MHCV demand growth of 35% y-y "surprising positively", while tractors were also ahead. However, some OEMs faced logistical challenges, particularly on the export side, with some logistics constraints also seen in the domestic market.

As the sector enters the high-base second half of FY27, Nomura expects industry growth to moderate, although companies exposed to EVs and new model launches should continue to outperform. EV penetration reached 7.2% in PVs and 10.7% in two-wheelers in August, while penetration in three-wheelers crossed 50%.

Nomura said it continues to see India's EV market at an "inflection point", with underlying demand potentially 20-30% higher than sales as supply takes time to catch up. It cited waiting periods of six months for Tata Punch EV, around three months for M&M 9S and two-three months for Ather.

In PVs, industry wholesales rose 36% y-y to 447,000 units. Maruti Suzuki's overall volumes were below estimates, while Tata Motors' domestic PV sales rose 59% y-y to around 65,200 units. M&M's UV volumes increased around 50% to 59,000 units, while Hyundai's domestic sales rose 44% to 54,400 units, although exports were hit by logistical constraints linked to the West Asia conflict.

Two-wheeler volumes rose 10% y-y. Bajaj Auto's wholesales jumped 28% to 535,700 units, well above Nomura's estimate, while TVS Motor's total volumes rose 21% but missed estimates. Hero MotoCorp also fell short of expectations.
MHCV volumes grew 35% y-y. TMCV's total MHCV sales rose 29% to 19,000 units, ahead of Nomura's estimate, while Ashok Leyland's volumes increased 46% to 13,700 units, also above expectations.

title: Nomura retains 'Buy' on M&M, Hyundai, TMCV, TVS and Sonacom after strong August auto volumes
